note: FNS 1011 is an introductory framework section establishing three principles: (1) income verification procedures vary by source/type, (2) income is verified for the budget or issuance month depending on the household's budgeting and reporting requirements, and (3) some income must be verified for other months (e.g., student grants prorated over a period). The OLG covers the substance of all three through distributed content: the Verification Chart maps income types to required documents; 'Types of Earned Income > Verification of Income' details earned income verification (pay stubs, employer statements, self-employment records); the Simplified Reporting IR page specifies different verification rules for earned vs. unearned income (e.g., $125 threshold for unearned); and 'Unearned Income Overview > Mandatory Income Averaging' addresses student grant proration ('averaged over the period for which it was provided'). BEACON prospective budgeting procedures are documented for both earned and unearned income. However, the OLG lacks a consolidated overview explicitly stating the general framework that verification procedures are source-dependent and month-dependent. There is no single page explaining that the timing of verification (budget month vs. issuance month) depends on the household's budgeting and reporting system. Workers learn this implicitly through context-specific pages rather than through an explicit procedural framework.
